notes: Nine-transistor cascade drawn on a page rotated ~10 degrees clockwise, so every 'horizontal' run slopes down to the right and every 'vertical' run leans left going down; coordinates below are 512-space centres of the ink. All 9 BJTs are drawn the same way: a vertical base bar, the base lead leaving the middle of the bar perpendicular, and the collector/emitter leaving the two ends at ~45 degrees then routed orthogonally. In every PNP (0, 1, 21, 22) the UPPER 45-degree lead carries the arrowhead pointing into the bar and is the emitter; in every NPN (5, 8, 9, 15, 19) the LOWER lead carries the outward arrowhead and is the emitter. That reading also puts every NPN emitter on the ground rail and every PNP emitter toward a supply, as expected. Net map: 0 = the bottom rail plus GND 7. the column continues down to (326,355), right to (363,371), and down to the collector of BJT 19 at (351,406). n15 = collector of BJT 22 down from (404,326) to (387,417) then right to the base of BJT 15 at (410,419). Judgment calls: (a) THE CROSSING CONVENTION. This drafter uses no junction dots at all; instead the two crossings that are NOT connections are drawn with an unmistakable rectangular 'crossover' bulge — the wire steps sideways, runs past the other wire on the offset, and steps back. There are exactly two such bulges, verified at 14x and 18x: at (367,200), where the Diode 4 / Diode 12 column steps right from x=366 to x=372 and back to x=357 across the n4-n5 supply rail, and at (297,404), where the Resistor 6 column steps right from x=295 to x=302 and back to x=288 across the n10 wire. Both are read as crossings, NOT junctions. (b) The other two crossings in the drawing, at (266,188) and (417,218), carry no bulge and show continuous, slightly thickened ink at the intersection at 26x; they are read as 4-way junctions. Circuit sense supports both readings: at (266,188) the V-DC 11 arrow stem must land on the rail, and at (417,218) it puts the emitter of NPN 5 on the +5V node while its collector sits on +15V. It also confirms (a): if (297,404) were a junction, the bottom of Resistor 6 would drag net n10 onto ground, shorting collector to emitter on BJT 8 and grounding the base of BJT 19 — a degenerate reading the bulge explicitly rules out. (c) Components 7 (GND) and the 5 V-DC (one port) supply arrows are the only one-terminal parts; the arrows at +15V, +10V, +5V and +3V are labelled, the arrow at (270,166) (component 11) carries no label but is drawn identically and is treated the same. (d) Diode terminal order is upper-then-lower as drawn for both diodes; two-terminal order affects no metric. (e) No component was added, removed or re-classed; all 23 inventory entries were located in the ink.
